subject: Air-gapped enclave: concession & nonstandard access request — Hemisync
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hemisync Procurement <procurement@hemisync.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped enclave: initial commercial + access ask

Hi Olivia / procurement team,

Thanks again for the pilot discussion earlier this week. Hemisync's requirements were really clear — you want an in-region, air-gapped enclave in Western Canada with strict egress controls and no remote shell access to customer VMs. To make the deployment economics work for you we can offer a first-year concession on unit pricing but we need an internal sign-off for a couple of non-standard constraints.

Summary of Hemisync asks: 
- Dedicated, in-region enclave with no public network egress without explicit customer-approved pathway
- No vendor interactive shell or jump-host access; support via audited ticketing + ephemeral, customer-authorized sessions only
- Short audit window (customer requests 180 days of logs retained, with on-site audit allowed twice per year)

What we (Redwood) are asking for: 
- Approval to offer a 20% first-year revenue credit if Hemisync signs the 24-month commitment within 30 days
- Agreement to a narrow exception to our standard support access (ephemeral remote session allowed only with pre-approved runbook) and to document the operational escape clause for severe incidents
- Acceptance of an on-site audit cadence limited to one scheduled visit per 12 months plus one extraordinary visit with 14 days notice

Attachments: Hemisphere_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft)
Link: HubSpot deal (included below)

Next steps: can you and Legal confirm whether we have executive latitude to grant the 20% concession and the tighter access limitations? I can fast-track an updated SOW and redline the MSA once we have a thumbs-up.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Lead, West
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0137
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@hemisync.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped enclave: initial commercial + access ask

Marcus,

Appreciate the quick summary. A couple clarifying points from our procurement/IT security side:

- SOC 2 report and architectural diagram that shows the physical separation are required before Legal will sign anything.
- The ask to limit on-site audits to once per year is acceptable, but we will insist on 180 days of logs (or exportable logs) retained and an option to request a forensic audit with 7 days' notice in the event of suspected data leakage.
- Regarding vendor access: we cannot approve any remote shell access. Ephemeral sessions are acceptable but MUST be brokered through our on-prem jump gateway and only for predefined maintenance windows.

Procurement also flagged the 20% concession: the commercial team will need a written executive approval from Redwood to proceed with the MSA redline and to send it to our Legal for review.

Can you loop in your legal & deals team with recommended redlines? We'll hold off sending our legal's version until we see Redwood's suggested changes.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Hemisync Therapeutics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hemisync enclave ask — need exec ok for concession + access constraints

Kimberly / Karthik,

Fwd'ing Hemisync's reply. They want SOC2, diagram, 180-day logs retained, and zero remote-shell. Procurement wants our exec signoff in writing for the 20% concession.

My recommendation:
- Approve a 18% first-year concession (meets sales comp and keeps margin buffer)
- Allow the narrow, auditable ephemeral session model (brokered through customer's gateway) but add a strict supportability escape clause: Redwood can request temporary elevated access for up to 8 hours in the event of a critical incident with a recorded, customer-approved runbook and two-person Redwood audit trail
- Limit on-site audits to one scheduled visit per 12 months; extraordinary forensic audit only with mutual agreement AND only if customer presents clear evidence of data compromise (we push back on unconditional 7-day forensic audit)

Attachments for legal review: redlined-MSA-Hemisync.pdf (proposed redlines) and revised SOW in the drive link.

If Legal signs off on the language above, we need someone on Exec team to approve the 18% concession and the escape clause. Can Laura or someone on the commercial leadership side provide an ok?

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hemisync enclave ask — legal redlines attached

Marcus / Kimberly,

Reviewed Hemisync's requirements and Marcus' proposed approach. High-level notes from Legal/InfoSec review:

1) SOC2: provide the latest SOC2 Type II report and an architecture diagram. No problem.
2) Remote access: we should accept the ephemeral, customer-brokered session model but add explicit controls in the MSA:
   - All sessions logged and retained for 12 months
   - Session initiation requires written customer authorization for the specific window (email accepted)
   - Any session is recorded and hashed; telemetry exported to customer at month end
3) Audit / forensic: push back on unconditional forensic audit within 7 days. Recommend: one scheduled audit / 12 months, plus an extraordinary audit only upon showing of reasonable cause (for example, verified data exfiltration indicators). If extraordinary audit is agreed, require customer to cover reasonable third-party audit fees unless Redwood is found materially at fault.
4) Pricing concession: Legal defers commercial approval, but recommends cap at 18% for year one and require full prepayment or signed letter of credit for pilot enclave build cost.

I attached a redline (redlined-MSA-Hemisync.pdf) with the language above and a short risk memo. If Marcus can accept the edits and Kimberly confirms commercial appetite for 18%, I'm comfortable routing this to Laura for an exec sign-off with the specific conditions summarized here.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hemisync enclave ask — legal redlines attached

Team,

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I reviewed the risk memo and discussed with Ops leadership. Decision below — conditional approval only:

1) Commercial concession: Approve an 18% first-year revenue credit. Condition: Hemisync must sign a 24-month commitment and make the first 6 months' subscription payment upfront within 30 days of countersignature.
2) Access model: Accept the ephemeral session model, brokered through Hemisync's gateway. All sessions must be pre-approved via email ticket and recorded. Redwood retains a right to suspend access immediately if anomalous activity is detected.
3) Audits: Approve one scheduled on-site audit per 12 months. Extraordinary forensic audits require a documented showing of cause and Redwood's agreement; if Redwood is not materially at fault and an audit is requested, Hemisync will cover auditor fees.
4) Operational escape clause: Insert language in SOW/MSA that allows Redwood to perform emergency remediation (including temporary elevation of access) for up to 8 hours with post-facto customer notification if there is a clear, imminent threat to platform integrity.

Please finalize the redlined MSA and SOW, confirm the payment mechanics in the SOW, and send the agreement for DocuSign. Marcus — please relay these conditions to Hemisync and request SOC2 + architecture diagram.

Once legal prepares the final MSA with the agreed language, I will provide an exec sign-off email to attach to their countersigned copy.

Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
